name: BlackRock, Inc.
reason: Scale leader (iShares, Aladdin) but fee earnings track market levels, EPS sits at 1.0x its 10y peak, and the GIP/HPS/Preqin private-markets deals (acq/FCF 0.27) are a recent transformation that is hard to forecast.

name: Box, Inc.
reason: Mature content-management SaaS whose consensus FY1 EPS growth is only 6.9%; GAAP vs adjusted EPS gap averages 574% because of stock-based comp, and AI/hyperscaler bundling threatens the business; FCF yield of 7.6% is flattered by SBC.

name: Broadridge Financial Solutions, Inc.
reason: Near-monopoly proxy/investor-communications utility with 10/10 years of >=7% EPS growth (13.4% 10y CAGR), ROIC 15%, net debt/EBITDA 1.7x and recurring fee revenue at 16x NTM P/E.

name: BrightView Holdings, Inc.
reason: Commoditized commercial landscaping with 1.9% 10y revenue CAGR, 10y avg ROIC of 0.8% and EPS at 0.63x its peak; a cheap but ordinary business with no specialness.

name: Blackstone Inc.
reason: Alternative-asset earnings depend on realizations and capital-markets activity (EPS fell 24% in 2023; EBIT margin ranged 27-109%), and FCF conversion is 0.25, so 5-10y earnings cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: CACI International Inc
reason: Growth has been acquisition-led (acq/FCF 1.43x over 10y) with net debt/EBITDA of 4.45x, margin at its 10y high, and the business depends on US government budgets and contract recompetes.

name: Calix, Inc.
reason: Lumpy broadband-equipment cycle (EBIT margin swung from -21% to +11%; 2024 EPS -67%) tied to BEAD/carrier capex, with a GAAP vs adjusted gap of 178%.

name: Callaway Golf Company
reason: Discretionary golf/Topgolf hybrid with shares up 8.1% a year, acq/FCF 39.7x, net debt/EBITDA 4.2x and EPS at 0.12x its peak; fails on leverage and on growth via acquisition.

name: Carrier Global Corp.
reason: Recent portfolio transformation (Viessmann acquisition, divestitures) with net debt/EBITDA of 3.15x and only 2/5 years of >=7% EPS growth; housing/HVAC cyclicality makes the post-transformation earnings base hard to underwrite.

name: Maplebear Inc.
reason: Only 2 profitable years; faces credible competitive and disintermediation threats from DoorDash, Uber and Amazon and from grocers' own delivery, and the 10.5% FCF yield is helped by stock-based comp addbacks.

name: Central Bancompany, Inc.
reason: Conservative family-controlled Missouri bank but newly listed; consensus EPS growth is only 5-7% a year (FY2/FY3 6.8%/6.1%), 2025 EPS +26% was partly rate-driven, and nothing marks it out from a good ordinary bank.

name: CBL & Associates Properties, Inc.
reason: Post-bankruptcy mall REIT with revenue declining 5.8% a year and net debt/EBITDA of 6.9x; the 17% FCF yield reflects structural retail decline, not specialness.

name: Crown Castle Inc.
reason: Net debt/EBITDA of 10.5x, AFFO/share down 37% in 2025 after the fiber/small-cell sale, and carrier concentration (consolidated tenants) leaves no route to >=7% growth.

name: CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc
reason: Entrenched P&C-claims network but GAAP EPS is ~0 against a large adjusted figure (heavy SBC/amortization), net debt/EBITDA is 5.0x, and AI could disintermediate claims workflows.

name: Cadre Holdings, Inc.
reason: Niche law-enforcement safety products, but growth is acquisition-led (acq/FCF 1.05x), 5y EPS CAGR is -1.9%, and the 8.3% FCF yield rests on NTM consensus rather than a recurring record.

name: Celsius Holdings Incorporated
reason: Fad-prone energy-drink brand reliant on PepsiCo distribution (single dominant customer), with the Alani Nu acquisition (acq/FCF 1.98x), shares rising 9.9% a year and margin at a 10y high.

name: Chewy, Inc.
reason: Strong Autoship customer proposition, but EBIT margin is only 2.2% with negative ROIC history and Amazon/Walmart as competitors; FCF (9.6% NTM yield) is helped by SBC and working capital, so margin expansion is hard to forecast.

name: Cleveland-Cliffs Inc
reason: Commodity flat-rolled steel with negative 2024-25 EPS, LTM FCF yield of -14% (the NTM 9% FCF is not recurring) and shares up 12.7% a year from acquisitions.

name: Calumet, Inc.
reason: Refining-linked specialty/renewable-fuels producer with net debt/EBITDA of 9.2x and losses in 9 of 11 years; earnings depend on crack spreads and renewable-diesel credits.

name: Cummins Inc.
reason: Quality engine franchise but cyclical truck/power-gen earnings sit at their 10y peak (EPS 1.0x max, margin in the 100th percentile) after a data-center genset boom, and EPA27/electrification is a technology transition risk.
